rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - no criminal record inquiry before conditional offer
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not require a housing application with criminal record questions, or make any oral or written inquiry about an applicant's criminal record, before making a conditional offer. The applicant may provide evidence of inaccuracies in the record or of rehabilitation or other mitigating factors.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers offering rental dwelling units for residential purposes, other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: A provider may consider before a conditional offer whether the applicant was ever convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program. Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are not covered.
rules.penalty: Penalties not to exceed $1,000 with no prior violation within five years, not to exceed $5,000 with one other violation within five years, and not to exceed $10,000 with two or more other violations within seven years. The director may also order further actions, such as return of the rental application fee.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - disclosure before accepting application fee
rules.requirement: Before accepting any application fee, a housing provider must disclose in writing whether its eligibility criteria include review of criminal history. It must also state that the applicant may provide evidence of inaccuracies in the record or of rehabilitation or other mitigating factors.

rules.penalty: Penalties not to exceed $1,000, $5,000 or $10,000 depending on prior violations.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - criminal records that may never be considered
rules.requirement: Either before or after a conditional offer, a housing provider may not evaluate an applicant based on arrests or charges that did not result in conviction. The same applies to expunged, pardoned, vacated or nullified convictions, juvenile adjudications of delinquency, and sealed records.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - lookback limits after conditional offer
rules.requirement: After a conditional offer, a housing provider may consider only certain records. These are convictions for murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, specified sexual offenses or crimes requiring lifetime sex offender registration. They also include first-degree offenses within six years, second- or third-degree offenses within four years, and fourth-degree offenses within one year preceding the conditional offer.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - withdrawal of conditional offer
rules.requirement: A housing provider may withdraw a conditional offer based on criminal record only if it determines, by preponderance of the evidence, that withdrawal is necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate and nondiscriminatory interest, after an individualized assessment. It must give written notice of the specific reasons and an opportunity to appeal, and on request made within 30 days it must provide free copies of the information relied upon.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - advertisements excluding people with criminal records
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not knowingly or purposefully publish a housing advertisement stating that it will not consider applicants who have been arrested or convicted of crimes or offenses. It also may not use advertisements, application forms or inquiries expressing unlawful limitations as to criminal record.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers offering rental dwelling units for residential purposes, other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Except for drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and lifetime registration requirements under a State sex offender registration program.
rules.penalty: Penalties not to exceed $1,000, $5,000 or $10,000 depending on prior violations.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not knowingly or purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses, except for drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - no drug or alcohol testing of applicants
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test. It also may not request the applicant's consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
